skill.name: descriptive-action
skill.description: Use when the user asks to describe, summarize, analyze, compare, explain, or report on something (text, data, events, systems) without asking for recommendations or next steps.
skill.summary: Produce neutral, evidence-based descriptions and analysis without adding recommendations.
skill.author: BellaBe

security_audit.summary: The only static finding is a false positive. The cited line instructs the model to avoid normative language, which supports neutral analysis and does not request reconnaissance or sensitive system discovery.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 27 says "Avoid normative language," which is a neutral writing rule. It does not ask the assistant to inspect the host system, gather environment data, or bypass any boundary.

content.value_statement: Users often need neutral analysis without recommendations. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to separate facts, inferences, evidence, and unknowns.
actual_capabilities: Summarizes provided text, data, artifacts, or systems into concise descriptive points.
Separates directly supported facts from bounded inferences.
Organizes analysis into summary, details, evidence, and open questions.
Compares information without adding recommendations or strategy.
Identifies missing information that limits confidence.
limitations: Does not create action plans, recommendations, strategies, or next steps unless the user asks separately.
Cannot verify facts beyond the material and tools available in the active session.
May need source material or constraints to produce a reliable analysis.
Does not replace expert review for legal, medical, security, or financial decisions.

use_cases.title: Summarize Research Notes
use_cases.description: Turn long notes into neutral summaries with evidence and open questions.

use_cases.title: Compare Product Feedback
use_cases.description: Describe themes, differences, and constraints across user feedback without proposing product changes.

use_cases.title: Explain System Behavior
use_cases.description: Describe observed system behavior, relevant evidence, and unknowns for review.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Summary
prompt_templates.prompt: Summarize the following material neutrally. Separate facts, inferences, evidence, and open questions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a short article, memo, or note set.

prompt_templates.title: Structured Explanation
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain this material for [audience]. Use sections for summary, details, evidence, and open questions. Avoid recommendations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the output needs a clear structure for a specific audience.

prompt_templates.title: Comparative Analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these items using only the provided information. Describe similarities, differences, evidence, and uncertainty.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for product notes, documents, datasets, or project options.

prompt_templates.title: Bounded System Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the provided system observations. Identify supported findings, possible interpretations, evidence, constraints, and missing information.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for complex technical, operational, or data-driven reviews.

output_examples.input: A user provides meeting notes about delayed onboarding and asks for a neutral summary.
output_examples.output: The response lists the main delay themes, separates confirmed points from inferred causes, cites note excerpts, and names unresolved questions.

output_examples.input: A team provides two product feedback summaries and asks for a comparison.
output_examples.output: The response describes shared themes, distinct complaints, evidence strength, and gaps without recommending roadmap changes.

output_examples.input: An engineer provides logs and observations from a service incident.
output_examples.output: The response summarizes observed behavior, likely relationships, supporting evidence, constraints, and unknowns for follow-up analysis.

best_practices: Provide the source material, audience, timeframe, and scope before asking for analysis.
Ask for facts, inferences, evidence, and open questions when accuracy matters.
Request a comparison table or short sections when reviewing multiple inputs.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill when you need recommendations, strategy, or action steps.
Do not ask it to infer facts that are not supported by the provided material.
Do not omit important constraints such as audience, timeframe, or source quality.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It produces neutral summaries, explanations, comparisons, and analyses based on provided material.

faq.question: Does it give recommendations?
faq.answer: No. It avoids recommendations, next steps, and strategy unless the user makes a separate request.

faq.question: Can it analyze technical material?
faq.answer: Yes. It can describe systems, logs, artifacts, or observations when enough context is provided.

faq.question: How does it handle uncertainty?
faq.answer: It labels inferences, lists missing information, and avoids presenting unsupported claims as facts.

faq.question: Which tools support this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is this skill safe for marketplace use?
faq.answer: No evidence of malicious behavior was found in the reviewed skill file.
